title: AI retry and reopening remain blocked after a transient IndexedDB preparation failure; reload recovers
repro: 1. Open a fresh RN web page, enable Create AI Images and Customize AI Style, disable AI auto-save, and draw a stroke. Intercept every API endpoint using the AI-1 fixtures.
2. Simulate a full disk for the next saved AI job by refusing its IndexedDB write with QuotaExceededError. Open the wand and select Sticker. Observe the first error card and zero generation uploads.
3. Restore successful IndexedDB writes and press Try again. Observe Still not working, no further attempted write and zero generation uploads.
4. Choose Keep drawing, reopen the wand and select Sticker again. It fails again even though storage writes are restored.
5. Reload the page, draw again and select Sticker: the same success fixture now produces the AI result. Repeat in a second independent browser context.
expected: After a transient preparation-write failure ends, explicit retry or reopening should safely reconcile durable storage and allow a new run, or offer an actionable storage recovery path. No paid request should be retried automatically.
actual: The storage owner remains uncertain after the first refused put. Try again and reopening never reread it, so every subsequent prepare fails before another put or upload. The UI blames the picture-maker and suggests waiting. Reloading creates a fresh owner and generation succeeds. Both independent contexts recorded exactly one refused write, zero uploads before reload, and one successful fixture upload after reload.
suspectedCode: experiments/native-architecture/src/platform/aiStorageOwner.web.ts:114 rejects non-rereading work while uncertain; platform/aiStorage.web.ts:100 queues prepare without rereading; ai/generationFlow.ts:154 retries directly without reconciling storage.
shipping: Empirical comparison at the same commit: shipping generates the fixture image successfully with all IndexedDB puts refused after AI setup; zero puts are attempted during that generation. Shipping has no equivalent durable preparation journal, so this comparison does not prove recovery at the RN-specific write boundary. See reference-quota.json.

surface: web-webkit 26.6 and web-firefox 155.0 on macOS; phone, tablet, desktop matrix failures; two independent public phone reproductions per engine
title: WebKit and Firefox cannot create AI pictures because RN rejects metadata in its own captured PNGs
repro: 1. Serve the RN export with coloring assets on 127.0.0.1. Connect WebKit 26.6 or Firefox 155.0 and serve the recorded API fixture; use a fresh browser context.
2. Open Settings → AI Art. Enable Create AI Images and Customize AI Style; disable Auto-Save AI Images. Close Settings and draw one stroke.
3. Tap Create AI image and choose Sticker. Instead of a picture, observe Hmm, that didn’t work and Try again. The fixture sees a free-grant request but no generation upload.

4. Repeat in a second fresh context. Run repro/ai-webkit-diagnostic.mjs with HUNT_ENGINE=webkit or HUNT_ENGINE=firefox to capture the browser-generated PNGs. Run repro/read-webkit-png.mjs for WebKit, or HUNT_ENGINE=firefox node repro/read-original-png.mjs for Firefox, from the campaign folder paths shown in README.
expected: A drawing captured by the app in a supported browser can reach the recorded success reply and show its result card. Valid browser-added PNG metadata must not make the app reject its own captured drawing.
actual: Two independent public flows per engine stop before any AI preparation write or generation upload. WebKit canvas PNGs contain eXIf before image data; Firefox canvas PNGs contain a 16-byte deBG chunk after IDAT. The real originalImageGrid rejects all six captured PNGs per engine. Removing only the respective metadata chunk makes each image pass with its original dimensions; Sharp also decodes the original files. Mozilla encoder source independently confirms deBG after IDAT is a Firefox encoder feature; no browser preference was changed. This does not establish every Firefox configuration. The initial matrix shows pre-upload failures at all three primary profiles in each engine. Downstream AI retry/report/poll/quota checks remain blocked by this input failure and are not separate defects.
suspectedCode: experiments/native-architecture/src/drawing/CaptureSvg.web.tsx:186 captures the browser PNG; platform/aiStorage.web.ts:66 admits that original; ai/pngResult.ts:65 rejects eXIf and ai/pngResult.ts:92 rejects metadata after IDAT, including Firefox deBG.
shipping: Same-commit shipping web in both supplied engines completes the public flow with the recorded API fixture: one generation POST and a visible Download action. Firefox sends a 3738-byte WebP, 780x1538, in its comparison. WebKit uses PNG; its remote request receipt does not expose payload bytes, so only fixture-backed UI success is claimed there. See webkit-reference-ai.json and firefox-reference-ai.json. No hosted delivery or physical iOS behavior is claimed.

surface: RN web Chromium 153.0.8010.12, WebKit 26.6, Firefox 155.0; JavaScript disabled
title: Canonical section URLs and the footer release link lose their targets without JavaScript
repro: 1. Build npm run build:site and use the file/pretty-URL/404 fixture host on 127.0.0.1:6150.
2. In a fresh 390x844 context with JavaScript disabled, open /privacy and activate the footer What's new link.
3. Observe /changelog#release-1-6-0, then inspect the target or its scroll position.

4. Repeat in a fresh context. Direct /privacy#contact, /changelog#release-1-0-0 and /design#dottie show the same defect. A phone-light suffixed privacy link opened at desktop dark instead targets a hidden variant.
expected: A page link or canonical shared section URL reaches its visible section with scripts disabled. A copied section address retains its meaning at another viewport or theme.
actual: The prerenderer changes every linked section id to id~layout-theme, but canonical URLs and cross-document footer links still use the unsuffixed id. The requested element does not exist, so navigation opens at the page top instead of the requested section. A suffixed address copied from another layout/theme finds only a hidden target. Same-variant in-page contents links work; JavaScript-enabled visits normalize the suffix and work.
suspectedCode: tools/migration/prerender-native-web-pages.mjs:197 (withVariantFragments renames the targets; pageBootScript can normalize only when JavaScript runs)
shipping: The rebuilt SvelteKit reference at the same candidate source reaches the canonical privacy, oldest-release and design sections and the footer release target without JavaScript. Verified twice in Chromium, WebKit and Firefox; visible target tops are approximately 96px for information pages and 160px for design.

surface: RN web Chromium 153.0.8010.12, WebKit 26.6 and Firefox 155.0; 320x740; light/dark; JavaScript on/off
title: Admin masthead overflows at 320 px and clips its brand suffix
repro: 1. Build the site and open /admin in a fresh 320x740 context.
2. Observe the right end of the masthead, and compare document.documentElement.scrollWidth with innerWidth.
3. Repeat in a fresh context; also check light/dark and JavaScript on/off.
expected: The masthead stays within the 320 px viewport and its Admin suffix remains fully visible, as on the rebuilt SvelteKit page.
actual: The two fixed-width masthead links plus their gap exceed the sheet width. The brand link ends at about x323.47 and the document scroll width is 323 px. The rightmost suffix pixels are clipped and the right gutter is lost. Functional fixture sign-in, stats, add/remove, reload and sign-out still pass.
suspectedCode: experiments/native-architecture/src/pageDocument/admin/adminChrome.tsx:81 (single-row topbar, fixed back-link and brand widths)
shipping: The rebuilt SvelteKit /admin stays exactly 320 px wide in all corresponding captures. It drops the crayon strip at this width and keeps the complete Admin suffix inside the right gutter.

surface: RN web and rebuilt SvelteKit /design; Chromium, WebKit, Firefox; light theme; JavaScript disabled
title: No-script design page loses the selected segment backing and washes out its label
repro: 1. Open /design in a fresh light-theme 390x844 context with JavaScript disabled.
2. Inspect the selected Light option in the header theme picker.
3. Repeat in a fresh context and compare the same control with JavaScript enabled.
expected: The prerendered specimen has a readable selected label and visibly represents its selected state even when no script can measure a moving thumb.
actual: The selected label is white on the rgb(233, 233, 233) track, approximately 1.21:1 contrast. RN renders no selected backing without measured cells; SvelteKit renders a zero-width thumb. JavaScript-enabled controls paint the purple backing. This is a static visual defect, not a claim that the preview control can operate without JavaScript.
suspectedCode: experiments/native-architecture/src/rsdDrawing/RsdSegmentedPicker.tsx:286 (thumb needs a measured cell; segmentActive at line 452 uses on-brand ink without a static backing)
shipping: The rebuilt SvelteKit page has the same no-script defect in all three engines, twice each. Its selected thumb has zero width. Recorded as a shared pre-existing polish issue, not an RN-only regression.

surface: RN web /design; Chromium 153.0.8010.12, WebKit 26.6, Firefox 155.0; 1280x800; JavaScript on/off
title: The desktop design sidebar scrolls its last Contents label below the viewport
repro: 1. Open /design at 1280x800 in a fresh context and let the fonts load.
2. Keep the main document at the top, put the pointer over the left Contents sidebar and wheel down to the sidebar’s maximum scroll position.
3. Observe that the last label, Dottie, is entirely below the 800 px viewport. Repeat in a second fresh context.
expected: The sidebar’s complete final label fits inside the visible scrolling area when the sidebar reaches its own bottom, as it does in the rebuilt SvelteKit page.
actual: The sticky sidebar begins at y64 but its padded box is 792 px tall and ends at y856. At its maximum scrollTop of 441, the Dottie text lies around y802–820, entirely below the viewport. Its anchor retains a small visible hit area, which Playwright can click; this is a hidden navigation label, not a completely unreachable section. The corresponding page section and local fragment work.
suspectedCode: experiments/native-architecture/src/pageDocument/design/DesignDocument.tsx:104 (content-box maxHeight excludes the sidebar’s vertical padding)
shipping: The rebuilt SvelteKit sidebar’s scroll container ends at y776 and contains the Dottie label after reaching its bottom. Chromium/WebKit text bounds are approximately y721–739; Firefox reaches the same range after a second wheel completes its scroll. All corresponding last-link clicks succeed.
